# Bounded foundation-history follow-up

The previous common-One bridge pilot remains closed negative. This asks one
remaining question:does the curriculum work better when the model already
learned to use recurrence during pretraining? It is an explicitly adaptive
follow-up on consumed discovery DEV,not independent confirmation or a repair
that changes the old result.

## Foundations and controls

Retain original scientific seed5231 checkpoints from the same random initializer:
R at1.004887590B targets;One at the same source exposure;and the stronger One at
1.237788282B targets,approximately matched to R's retained pretraining work.
Verify complete original states/roles,digests and equal prediction inventory.
Remove only the closed training-only head;reset every adaptation optimizer.
Never adopt a fitted qualification or previous curriculum state.

Execute seven cooled endpoints:One-work/NTP andOne-work/bridge;R/NTP andR/bridge;
One-source/NTP andOne-source/bridge;plus a longer One-work/bridge control. The
basic arms receive200 updates. The longer One endpoint is245 updates,computed
from the complete retained pretraining-plus-adaptation matrix budget before
this study. That leaves0.00961% unused full-trajectory work;the next update
would exceed it. Retained update trajectories are separate from prior tuning,
discarded branches and total development receipts,which remain preserved.

All basic continuations see identical128-window NTP updates beginning at source
window1,210,880,beyond every parent's cursor. R andOne-source did not consume the
intervening One-work pretraining targets. Their entire source histories match;
One-work's longer history is the resource control. This new shared slice differs
from the old pilot,so cross-study changes are not a pure causal history estimate.

## Fixed learning and execution

Keep the identical1,618 original worked problems,view construction,task order
(seed40009),noise policy,ordered normal-decoder loss and curriculum. Each bridge
update uses128 original task views and128 NTP windows. Loss is mean source NTP
plus0.3 mean original-answer CE plus0.03 per-example artificial task-EOS CE.
All original math text/steps/answers remain source substrings;no calculator
labels,teacher model,generated examples or RL. First quarter shows all original
work,second quarter its first half,final half none. Keep ordinary NTP throughout.

One always uses one pass;R cycles4,1,2 synchronized terminal passes with full
backpropagation. Same0.001 peak LR,10-update warmup,half-endpoint cooldown to
10% of peak;no HPO or additional rate/weight/depth/epoch search. The longer One
gets its own245-update curriculum/cooldown and may share only the identical
first stable update with its200-update parent. Never extend a cooled endpoint.

Freeze exact sources,data,parents,endpoints and ports before updates. Every
basic case first stops after one actual registered update. Require independent
pinned-upstream FP32 complete128-window NTP and applicable128-task gradients,
all families within2%,component loss agreement0.003 and independent clipping/
optimizer/moment checks. Count first updates as research even if a gate fails.
Only then continue from exact model/optimizer/per-rank RNG restoration. Verify
all32 replicas and complete source/task/matrix counters. Bit-exact future
trajectories are not assumed. Record100 actual warm updates20–119.

warm updates take0.39–0.61s;reserve2s/update plus launch/CPU overhead. Overall

135-task/115-group consumed discovery panel,no-work prompts,prefix-only fixed
